title: Erosion Control Works Act
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to contribute to promoting the public interest and industrial development by efficiently implementing erosion control works to prevent degradation of the national territory, protect people's lives and property from landslides and other hazards, and conserve the national territory. <Amended 2013.8.13>
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 2 (Definitions) The terms used in this Act mean the following: <Amended 2013.8.13, 2016.12.27, 2020.2.18>
1. “Degraded land” means an area where mountainous land (including other land; the same applies hereinafter) collapses, soil, stones, trees, etc. flow out, or sand drifts due to natural or human causes, and where restoration works are needed to conserve the national territory, prevent disasters, create landscapes, or enhance water-source recharge.
2. “Erosion control works” means works to install artificial structures or sow or plant vegetation to restore degraded land or prevent or avert the collapse of mountainous land, the outflow of soil, stones, trees, etc., or drifting sand, or incidental works to create landscapes or enhance water-source recharge.
3. “Erosion control facilities” means artificial structures installed and vegetation sown or planted through erosion control works (including vegetation already growing in the area where such works are implemented before their implementation).
4. “Erosion control area” means an area where erosion control works have been or are to be implemented, designated and publicly notified under Article 4 by the Special Metropolitan City Mayor, a Metropolitan City Mayor, the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, a Do Governor, or the Special Self-Governing Province Governor (hereinafter referred to as “Mayor/Do Governor”), or the head of a regional forest service.
5. “Landslide” means the sudden collapse of mountainous land due to natural or human causes.
6. “Debris flow” means the rapid outflow of soil, stones, trees, etc. mixed with water from mountainous land or valleys.
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 3 (Classification of Erosion Control Works) Erosion control works are classified according to their target areas as follows: <Amended 2013.8.13>
1. Mountain erosion control works: The following erosion control works implemented on mountainous land:
(a) Landslide prevention works: Erosion control works implemented to prevent landslides;
(b) Landslide restoration works: Erosion control works implemented to restore areas where landslides have occurred;
(c) Mountain conservation works: Erosion control works implemented to prevent the collapse or erosion of mountainous land or the outflow of soil and stones;
(d) Mountain restoration works: Erosion control works implemented to restore mountainous land damaged by natural or human causes.
2. Coastal erosion control works: The following erosion control works implemented in areas adjoining the coast, including coastal sand dunes:
(a) Coastal disaster prevention forest establishment works: Erosion control works implemented to reduce damage from storm surges, wind waves, drifting sand, salinity, etc.;
(b) Coastal erosion prevention works: Erosion control works implemented to prevent coastal erosion caused by waves, etc. or restore eroded coasts.
3. Torrent erosion control works: The following erosion control works implemented in mountain valleys, streams connected to mountainous land, or rivers:
(a) Mountain stream conservation works: Erosion control works implemented to reduce mountain stream flow velocity and prevent erosion and debris flows;
(b) Mountain stream restoration works: Erosion control works implemented to restore mountain streams damaged by natural or human causes;
(c) Erosion control dam installation works: Erosion control works to install small dams across mountain streams to reduce their gradient and prevent erosion, intercept soil, stones, trees, etc. and debris flows coming from upstream, and enhance water-source recharge.
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 3-2 (Master Plans for Erosion Control Works)
(1) The Administrator of the Korea Forest Service shall formulate and implement a master plan for erosion control works (hereinafter referred to as “master plan”) every five years, containing the following matters, to promote erosion control works in a planned and systematic manner:
1. Basic objectives and direction for erosion control works;
2. Matters concerning the promotion of development and utilization of erosion control technology;
3. Matters concerning sites for erosion control works and follow-up management;
4. Matters concerning the training of technical personnel for erosion control works;
5. Matters concerning the expansion of international exchanges in erosion control technology;
6. Other matters deemed necessary by the Administrator of the Korea Forest Service.
(2) A master plan may be amended where there are grounds for significant changes in the conditions for erosion control works, economic circumstances, etc.
(3) When intending to formulate or amend a master plan under paragraphs (1) and (2), the Administrator of the Korea Forest Service shall hear the opinions of the heads of relevant administrative agencies and Mayors/Do Governors; upon formulating or amending it, the Administrator shall notify its details to Mayors/Do Governors or heads of regional forest services without delay and publicly notify its outline.
(4) Mayors/Do Governors and heads of regional forest services shall formulate and implement regional erosion control works plans every five years according to the master plan, taking account of the characteristics of the areas under their jurisdiction. <Newly inserted 2013.8.13>
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]
[Title amended 2013.8.13]

Article 3-3 (Surveys of the Actual Conditions of Degraded Land)
(1) The Administrator of the Korea Forest Service shall conduct a basic survey of the actual conditions of degraded land every five years and reflect the results in the master plan to promote erosion control works efficiently. <Amended 2013.8.13>
(2) Based on the results of the basic survey under paragraph (1), the Administrator of the Korea Forest Service may conduct detailed surveys of areas where heavy rainfall, etc. may cause changes in topography or damage to ecosystems or living areas. <Amended 2013.8.13>
(3) The Administrator of the Korea Forest Service may request the heads of relevant administrative agencies, Mayors/Do Governors, and heads of Si/Gun/Gu (the head of a Gu means the head of an autonomous Gu; the same applies hereinafter) to provide necessary data for efficiently conducting surveys under paragraphs (1) and (2). In such cases, a person requested to provide data shall comply unless there is a special reason not to do so. <Newly inserted 2013.8.13>
(4) The details and methods of surveys under paragraphs (1) and (2), and other necessary matters, shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs. <Amended 2013.3.23, 2013.8.13>
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 4 (Designation of Erosion Control Areas)
(1) Erosion control areas shall be designated by Mayors/Do Governors or heads of regional forest services as prescribed by Presidential Decree. In such cases, they shall hear the opinions of the heads of Si/Gun/Gu and, where expropriation of land, etc. is necessary under Article 10-2, those of the owners, possessors, or interested parties of the land, etc.; when intending to designate an erosion control area in which torrent erosion control works under Article 3, subparagraph 3 are to be implemented on a river under the River Act, they shall consult in advance with the river management authority. <Amended 2013.8.13>
(2) Upon designating an erosion control area under paragraph (1), a Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a regional forest service shall publicly notify that fact without delay and notify the details of the designation to the owners, possessors, or interested parties of the land, etc. The same applies where a publicly notified area is changed or the designation of an erosion control area is cancelled. <Amended 2013.8.13>
(3) Where a site subject to designation as an erosion control area under paragraph (1) does not exceed the scale prescribed by Presidential Decree, it need not be designated as an erosion control area.
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 5 (Implementation of Erosion Control Works)
(1) Erosion control works shall be national projects.
(2) Erosion control works implemented as national projects under paragraph (1) (hereinafter referred to as “national erosion control works”) shall be implemented by Mayors/Do Governors or heads of regional forest services as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 6 (Implementation of Erosion Control Works by Persons Other than the State)
(1) Notwithstanding Article 5, local governments, public organizations, and other persons other than the State may implement erosion control works. In such cases, a person intending to implement erosion control works shall submit an erosion control works plan prescribed by Presidential Decree to the Mayor/Do Governor or the head of the regional forest service.
(2) Where a Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a regional forest service receives an erosion control works plan under paragraph (1) and deems it appropriate, he or she shall designate and publicly notify an erosion control area under Article 4: Provided, That where the relevant works are torrent erosion control works under the latter part of Article 4 (1), he or she shall consult with the river management authority about the area in which the works are to be implemented before designating and publicly notifying the erosion control area.
(3) When designating and publicly notifying an erosion control area under paragraph (2), a Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a regional forest service may attach conditions necessary for disaster prevention, etc.
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 6-2 (Establishment of a Database for Maintenance and Management of Erosion Control Dams)
(1) The Administrator of the Korea Forest Service may establish and operate a database containing the year of construction, specifications, and whether safety inspections have been conducted, etc. for erosion control dams (hereinafter referred to as “database”) for their systematic maintenance, management, and safety inspection.
(2) The Administrator of the Korea Forest Service may request the heads of relevant administrative agencies or Mayors/Do Governors to submit data necessary for establishing and operating the database. In such cases, the heads of relevant administrative agencies or Mayors/Do Governors so requested shall comply unless there is a special reason not to do so.
(3) Where necessary to establish and operate the database efficiently, the Administrator of the Korea Forest Service may entrust its establishment and operation to a specialized institution.
(4) Matters necessary for establishing and operating the database and for entrustment under paragraph (3) shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs.
[This Article newly inserted 2015.2.3]

Article 7 (Bearing of Expenses) Expenses incurred in implementing erosion control works shall be borne by the State: Provided, That where a local government, public organization, or another person other than the State implements such works under Article 6, the implementer shall bear the expenses, but the State may subsidize all or part thereof.
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 7-2 (Design and Construction of Erosion Control Works)
(1) When intending to implement erosion control works, a Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a regional forest service shall design and construct them in consideration of the conservation of the national territory, disaster prevention, landscape creation, or water-source recharge.
(2) Matters necessary for standards for the design and construction of erosion control works under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs. <Amended 2013.3.23>
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 7-3 (Feasibility Assessment of Erosion Control Works)
(1) When intending to implement erosion control works, a Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a regional forest service shall assess in advance their overall feasibility in terms of necessity, suitability, environmental compatibility, etc. (hereinafter referred to as “feasibility assessment”), taking account of the master plan and landslide-prone areas under Article 22 of the Forest Disaster Prevention Act: Provided, That a feasibility assessment may be omitted where erosion control works are implemented to restore damage from landslides or other natural disasters. <Amended 2013.8.13, 2025.1.31>
(2) The standards, methods, and projects subject to feasibility assessment, and other necessary matters, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 8 (Assignment of Forest Engineering Technicians)
(1) A person implementing erosion control works of at least the scale prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs (including a person entrusted to implement works under Article 26) shall assign a forest engineering technician from among forest technicians under Article 8 of the Act on the Promotion and Management of Forest Technology to guide and perform duties concerning the preparation and implementation of erosion control works plans. <Amended 2013.3.23, 2017.11.28>
(2) Matters necessary for the assignment of forest engineering technicians, etc. shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs. <Amended 2013.3.23>
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 9 (Investigations by Public Officials)
(1) Where necessary to investigate or survey national erosion control works, a Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a regional forest service may have public officials under his or her authority enter another person's land or alter or remove standing trees, bamboo, soil, stones, or other obstacles.
(2) A public official entering another person's land or altering or removing obstacles under paragraph (1) shall carry identification indicating his or her authority and present it to persons concerned.
(3) Where necessary to implement national erosion control works, a Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a regional forest service may perform any of the following acts on erosion control areas and nearby land, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. In such cases, Articles 14, 15, 15-2, and 25 (1) of the Mountainous Districts Management Act and Article 36 (1) and (5) of the Creation and Management of Forest Resources Act shall not apply. <Amended 2013.8.13, 2020.2.18, 2022.12.27>
1. Temporary use as a material stockyard or temporary road;
2. Alteration of land form and quality or installation of artificial structures;
3. Collection of standing trees, bamboo, soil, stones, turf, or grass.
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 10 (Compensation for Loss)
(1) Where a person suffers loss due to an act under Article 9 (1) or (3), the Mayor/Do Governor or the head of the regional forest service shall compensate for such loss as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2013.8.13>
(2) Where necessary to implement erosion control works under Article 3, erosion control areas and nearby land may be purchased or exchanged within budgetary limits through consultation with the landowner or upon the landowner's application, applying Article 26 of the Forest Disaster Prevention Act mutatis mutandis. <Newly inserted 2013.8.13; amended 2025.1.31>
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]
[Title amended 2013.8.13]

Article 10-2 (Expropriation and Use of Land, etc.)
(1) Where necessary to implement erosion control works under Article 3, a Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a regional forest service may expropriate land, objects, or rights within the project area (hereinafter referred to as “land, etc.”) (including use; the same applies hereinafter).
(2) Where an erosion control area has been designated and publicly notified under Article 4, project approval and public notification thereof under Articles 20 (1) and 22 of the Act on Acquisition of and Compensation for Land, etc. for Public Works Projects shall be deemed to have been granted and made.
(3) Except as otherwise expressly provided in this Act, the Act on Acquisition of and Compensation for Land, etc. for Public Works Projects shall apply mutatis mutandis to expropriation under paragraph (1).
[This Article newly inserted 2013.8.13]

Article 11 (Determination of Compensation) With regard to compensation for loss under Article 10, the Mayor/Do Governor or the head of the regional forest service and the person who suffered the loss shall consult with each other.
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 12 (Application for Adjudication) Where consultation under Article 11 fails or cannot be conducted, an application for adjudication may be filed with the competent land expropriation committee under Article 51 of the Act on Acquisition of and Compensation for Land, etc. for Public Works Projects, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 13 (Prohibition of Refusal of Erosion Control Works) No person shall refuse or obstruct the implementation of erosion control works or the management of erosion control facilities.
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 14 (Restrictions on Activities in Erosion Control Areas)
(1) No person shall fell standing trees or bamboo, collect soil, stones, tree roots, or grass roots, graze livestock, or otherwise damage or alter erosion control facilities or change the form and quality of land in an erosion control area without permission from the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, the Special Self-Governing Province Governor, the head of a Si/Gun/Gu, or the head of a regional forest service: Provided, That this shall not apply where river works are implemented under the River Act or permission to occupy a river area has been obtained. <Amended 2016.12.27>
(2) Upon receiving an application for permission under the main clause of paragraph (1), the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, the Special Self-Governing Province Governor, the head of a Si/Gun/Gu, or the head of a regional forest service shall grant permission unless the proposed activities fall under any of the following: <Amended 2016.12.27, 2020.2.18>
1. Damaging or altering the original form of basic artificial structures installed through erosion control works;
2. Felling standing trees or bamboo that are not damaged trees, where such felling impedes the purpose of designation of the erosion control area;
3. Collecting turf, grass, soil, or stones, or grazing livestock where soil outflow, etc. is expected to an extent that impedes achieving the purpose of designation of the erosion control area.
(3) Where permission under paragraph (2) has been obtained, permission under Articles 14, 15, 15-2, and 25 (1) of the Mountainous Districts Management Act and Article 36 (1) and (5) of the Creation and Management of Forest Resources Act shall be deemed to have been obtained, or a report thereunder deemed to have been filed. <Amended 2022.12.27>
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 15 (Management of Erosion Control Facilities)
(1) Erosion control facilities shall be managed by the person who implemented the erosion control works: Provided, That where the competent administrative authority under Article 5 of the Creation and Management of Forest Resources Act changes after implementation of the works, the new management entity shall manage the facilities. <Amended 2013.8.13>
(2) Where necessary to ensure the safety of erosion control facilities, the manager under paragraph (1) shall conduct inspections and safety diagnoses and take safety measures based on the results.
(3) Matters necessary for the management, inspection, safety diagnosis, and safety measures for erosion control facilities under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 16 (Bearing of Management Expenses) Expenses necessary for managing erosion control facilities shall be borne by their manager.
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 17 (Attribution of Benefits) A Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a regional forest service may pay benefits arising from erosion control facilities installed through national erosion control works to the owner or possessor of the erosion control area or the manager of the facilities, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 18 Deleted. <2006.12.28>

Article 19 Deleted. <2011.7.14>

Article 20 (Cancellation of Designation of Erosion Control Areas)
(1) Where an erosion control area falls under any of the following, a Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a regional forest service may cancel its designation as prescribed by Presidential Decree. In such cases, the opinions of the head of the Si/Gun/Gu shall be heard:
1. Where deemed necessary for a project directly operated by the State or a local government;
2. Where deemed necessary for a project encouraged as a policy of the State or a local government;
3. Where deemed necessary for public works under Article 4 of the Act on Acquisition of and Compensation for Land, etc. for Public Works Projects;
4. Where deemed necessary for collecting soil and stones for a project prescribed by Presidential Decree;
5. Where the purpose of designation of the erosion control area prescribed by Presidential Decree has been achieved;
6. Where the purpose of designation of the erosion control area prescribed by Presidential Decree has ceased to exist.
(2) Where a Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a regional forest service cancels the designation of an erosion control area under paragraph (1), he or she shall publicly notify that fact.
(3) Where the designation of an erosion control area is cancelled under paragraph (1), a Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a regional forest service may transfer erosion control facilities installed through national erosion control works to the owner of the land without charge, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 21 (Reimbursement of Expenses) A person intending to obtain cancellation of the designation of an erosion control area for a project under Article 20 (1) 2 through 4 shall reimburse the manager of the erosion control facilities for expenses incurred in implementing the erosion control works and other expenses prescribed by Presidential Decree: Provided, That this shall not apply in cases prescribed by Presidential Decree.
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 22 (Free Inspection of Documents) Where necessary for implementing erosion control works, relevant public officials may inspect or copy necessary documents and drawings free of charge, or request the issuance of certified copies thereof, at the registry office, tax office, or office of the Special Self-Governing City, Special Self-Governing Province, Si/Gun/Gu (meaning an autonomous Gu), or Eup/Myeon having jurisdiction over the relevant erosion control area. <Amended 2016.12.27>
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 22-2 Deleted. <2025.1.31>

Article 22-3 Deleted. <2025.1.31>

Article 23 (Erosion Control Works by Local Governments) Articles 7-3, 9, 10, 10-2, 11, 12, 17, and 20 (3) shall apply mutatis mutandis to erosion control works implemented by local governments under Article 6 and to the management, etc. of erosion control facilities. In such cases, “Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a regional forest service” shall be construed as “head of a local government,” and “national erosion control works” as “erosion control works implemented by a local government.” <Amended 2016.12.27>
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 24 (Erosion Control Works by Public Organizations) Where a person other than the State or a local government implements erosion control works under Article 6, Articles 14, 15, 15-2, and 25 (1) of the Mountainous Districts Management Act and Article 36 (1) and (5) of the Creation and Management of Forest Resources Act shall not apply within the erosion control area in which the works are implemented. <Amended 2022.12.27>
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 24-2 (International Cooperation) The State or a local government may strengthen international cooperation in erosion control, including international exchanges of erosion control technology and information, training of international specialists, and international joint research and development, and provide the support necessary therefor.
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 24-3 (Development of Technology for Erosion Control Works)
(1) The State shall formulate and implement necessary policies, including research and development of erosion control works technology and education and publicity, to prevent landslides, debris flows, etc.
(2) The State and local governments may delegate or entrust research and development of erosion control works technology and education, etc. under paragraph (1) to institutions or organizations prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs.
(3) When delegating or entrusting under paragraph (2), the State or a local government may provide necessary administrative and financial support.
[This Article newly inserted 2013.8.13]

Article 25 (Delegation of Authority)
(1) Part of the authority of the Administrator of the Korea Forest Service under this Act may be delegated to Mayors/Do Governors or heads of regional forest services, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) Part of the authority of Mayors/Do Governors or heads of regional forest services under this Act may be delegated to heads of Si/Gun/Gu or heads of national forest management offices, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 26 (Entrustment of Works) A Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a regional forest service may entrust the implementation of erosion control works to a forestry cooperative or the National Forestry Cooperative Federation under the Forestry Cooperatives Act, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 27 (Penalties) A person who violates Article 14 (1) shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than five years or a fine not exceeding 50 million won. <Amended 2016.12.27>
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]

Article 28 (Penalties) A person who violates Article 13 shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than one year or a fine not exceeding 10 million won. <Amended 2016.12.27>
[Wholly amended 2011.7.14]
